knowledge:
- key_parameters: varNames=A vector of parameter/column names in the input data that need to be analyzed ;; MaxN=The maximum number of clusters to consider during the merging process ;; x=The input flow cytometry data matrix or data frame
- alternatives: Model-based population identification methods (flowMeans is preferred for faster runtime without decreasing accuracy) ;; Standard k-means (flowMeans builds on k-means but allows multiple clusters to represent a single non-spherical population)
- when_to_use: When performing automated gating and cell population identification on high-throughput flow cytometry data, especially when populations are non-spherical.
- pitfalls: The user must ensure that no extra parameters (such as time or ID columns) are passed to the flowMeans function via varNames, as the function will not automatically remove them.

workflows.name: flow_cytometry_gating
workflows.intent: Identify and visualize cell populations in flow cytometry data using non-parametric clustering and change point detection.
input: flow_data.csv (matrix or data frame of flow cytometry measurements with marker channels)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and input data ;; 2. Run the flowMeans clustering algorithm on specified marker channels ;; 3. Plot the minimum distances between merged clusters ;; 4. Detect the optimal number of clusters using changepointDetection and plot the change point ;; 5. Visualize the final cluster memberships in 2D and multi-dimensional plots
workflows.code:
library(flowMeans)
data(x)
res <- flowMeans(x, varNames=c("FL1.H", "FL2.H", "FL3.H", "FL4.H"), MaxN=10)
plot(x[,c(3,4)], col=res@Labels[[1]], pch=20);
plot(res@Mins, xlab='Iteration', ylab='Distance')
plot(res@Mins, xlab=' ', ylab=' ', xlim=c(1, res@MaxN), ylim=c(0, max(res@Mins)))
ft<-changepointDetection(res@Mins)
abline(ft$l1)
abline(ft$l2);
par(new=TRUE)
plot(ft$MinIndex+1, res@Mins[ft$MinIndex+1], col='red', xlab='Iteration', ylab='Distance', xlim=c(1, res@MaxN), ylim=c(0, max(res@Mins)), pch=19);
plot(x, res, c("FL1.H", "FL2.H"))
plot(x, res, c("FL1.H", "FL2.H","FL3.H", "FL4.H"),pch='.')
